note: Party lines for the deviation analysis. Republican line: the general attitude of the Trump administration. Democratic line: the general attitude of the incoming Democratic congressional leaders. Leaders not yet elected or sworn in are treated as leaders.

parties.referenceActors: The Trump administration (President Trump and White House AI policy)

positions.summary: Use federal power to stop states from regulating AI: a litigation task force against state AI laws, funding leverage, and a push for preemptive federal legislation with a child-safety carve-out.

evidence.summary: Executive order "Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence" creates a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws, ties some federal funding to state AI policy, and tasks the White House AI adviser with proposing federal legislation that broadly preempts state AI laws, with carve-outs for child safety.

source.title: The White House: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence (executive order, Dec. 11, 2025)

evidence.summary: Text of the executive order.

positions.summary: Build data centers fast: faster federal permitting, a voluntary industry pledge on power costs, and opposition to local resistance, framed as helping China.

evidence.summary: Executive order accompanying the AI Action Plan speeds federal permitting for data center infrastructure and opens some federal and military land.

source.title: White House fact sheet: President Trump accelerates federal permitting of data center infrastructure (July 23, 2025)

evidence.summary: Ratepayer Protection Pledge, introduced in the State of the Union: large AI companies commit to cover the added power and grid costs of their new data centers and to negotiate separate rate structures. The pledge is voluntary and not binding.

source.title: White House: Ratepayer Protection Pledge (March 2026)

evidence.summary: Trump wrote that the only reason to reject data centers is wanting "to end up being backwards and poor" and that "China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement."

source.title: The Spokesman-Review: Trump slams opposition to data centers

evidence.summary: Trump urged the Senate to pass a permitting bill that he said codifies his Ratepayer Protection Pledge, adding "Remember, China will take any Data Center that we don't want, and pay lots of money for it."

source.title: Reuters: US Congress gets first post-Blue Wave crack at data centers with permitting bill (Nov. 9, 2026)

positions.summary: Allow licensed sales of advanced AI chips to China in exchange for a government revenue share.

evidence.summary: After halting Nvidia H20 exports to China in April 2025, the administration told Nvidia in July 2025 that export licenses would be granted; Nvidia said it hoped to start deliveries soon.

source.title: Nvidia: CEO Jensen Huang promotes AI in Washington, D.C. and China (July 2025)

evidence.summary: Commerce began reviewing licenses to export Nvidia H200, AMD MI325X and similar chips to China case by case, carrying out the president's December 2025 decision; the government's 25% share is collected through a separate tariff, not a license fee.

source.title: Bureau of Industry and Security: Commerce revises license review policy for semiconductors exported to China (Jan. 13, 2026)

positions.summary: Light-touch rules for AI developers: remove regulatory barriers and rely on voluntary commitments rather than binding safety mandates.
